part.text:
Now I understand the structure. This is a Next.js 16 app with PPR enabled (`cacheComponents: true`). **The problem:** `page.tsx:11` does a top-level `await getDashboardData()`, which blocks the *entire* page. There's no static shell — the whole `
` body is dynamic, so PPR can't prerender anything beyond the layout. The `loading.tsx` fallback is the only thing users see until the fetch resolves. **The fix:** Push data fetching down into each child component wrapped in ``, so the static shell (`

Dashboard

`) prerenders instantly and each card streams in independently with skeleton fallbacks. This is the standard Next.js PPR pattern. Let me create a todo list and implement.

part.text:
## Summary The problem was `page.tsx:11` doing a top-level `await getDashboardData()` — this blocked the **entire** page body, so PPR had no static shell to prerender (only the bare layout streamed, with users staring at `loading.tsx` until the fetch resolved). **What changed:** - `app/page.tsx` — converted to a synchronous component that renders the static shell (`

Dashboard

`) with each child wrapped in ``. The shell now prerenders instantly. - `app/CardStats.tsx`, `RevenueChart.tsx`, `LatestInvoices.tsx` — converted from sync prop-driven components to async self-fetching server components, so each becomes an independent dynamic hole that streams in on its own. - `app/skeletons.tsx` — added per-component skeleton fallbacks that become part of the prerendered shell, replaced by real content as each section resolves. The build confirms `/` is now `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML shell with dynamic server-streamed content, instead of a fully-blocked dynamic render.
